newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: SLOVENIA SKB BANK SAYS H1 CONSOL PROFIT DOWN.
newsitem.headline: SLOVENIA SKB BANK SAYS H1 CONSOL PROFIT DOWN.

text.p: Slovenia's second largest bank SKB said on Friday its consolidated pre-tax profit in the first six months of 1997 fell to 1.5 billion tolars ($8.7 million) from 1.8 billion in the same period of 1996.
"The main reasons for the fall were lower income from revaluation due to the lagging of foreign exchange rates behind domestic inflation and increased provisions," the bank said in a statement.
Consolidated balance sheet assets jumped to 225.7 billion tolars from 192.3 billion in the end of June 1996.
Net interest income fell to 4.0 billion tolars from 4.6 billion, while profit margins were down to 3.7 from 4.9 percent.

Net fee and commission income rose to 943 million tolars from 841 million, while net gains from dealing in foreign currencies jumped to 1.6 billion tolars from 217 million on account of the successful launch of two global depositary receipt (GDRs) issues in the first half of the year.
The bank issued its own GDRs in February and was intermediary in a GDR issue of shopping centre operator BTC in June. So far the two companies are the only Slovenian firms to have issued GDRs.
Provisions for loan losses rose to 1.8 billion tolars from 1.2 billion due to stricter regulation of the central bank.
Operating expenses rose by 9.5 percent and the number of staff was up by six percent because of three newly opened branches and expansion of commercial business.
The bank expects to open another four new units by the end of this year.
Unconsolidated pre-tax profit dropped to 1.7 billion tolars from 2.0 billion in the first half of 1996 while unconsolidated balance sheet assets rose to 215.9 billion tolars from 189.1 billion.
